items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: "Inf two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness, with retractions from low-trustworthiness sources entirely ineffective."
judge.evidence_topic: "Thie continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted."
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada em experimentos com retratação, sem indici os de temas políticos ou de saóde, está dentro do peródo 2018-2025 e é um estudo empórico com dados próprios.

items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments (N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated.
judge.evidence_topic: The Continued Influence Effect (CIE) is the phenomenon that retracted information often continues to influence judgments and inferences. [...] Participants read a fictitious news report in which original information and a retraction were each presented by either a source with high credibility or a source with low credibility.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada com materiais neutros (notícia fictícia) e dois experimientos com participantes humanos, alinhado ao pedido. O método descrito bate com o resumo, e o achado extraído é integralmente sustenado pelo resumo.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O resumo aborda o efeito de influência continuada e descreve dois experimentos com correções de desinformação, alinhando-se ao método extraído e sustentando o achado principal.

items.title: Don’t believe them! Reducing misinformation influence through source discreditation

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we tested whether immediate source discreditation could reduce people’s subsequent reliance on fictional event-related misinformation.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often continues to influence people’s reasoning even after it has been corrected.
judge.reason: O resumo trata diretamente do efeito de influência continuada (CIE), relata dois experimentos com desinformação fictícia sobre eventos, sem viés político ou de saúde, e os achados extraídos estão plenamente amparados pelo resumo.

items.title: Do the protective effects last? The effectiveness of alternative + forewarning/inoculation techniques in reducing misinformation reliance and reliance regression in the continued influence effect procedure

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 441), we aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the alternative explanation technique and a combination of an alternative explanation and a forewarning (Experiment 1) or inoculation (Experiment 2) in both reducing CIE and the effect of increasing misinformation reliance over time, which is called belief regression.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) refers to continued reliance on misinformation, even after it has been retracted.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que o estudo investiga o efeito de influência continuada com dois experimentos, manipulações de correção e medida de dependência da desinformação ao longo do tempo, e os achados relatados sustentam integralmente o achado principal extraído.

items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The results show that the reliability of corrections’ sources did not affect their processing when participants were not inoculated. However, inoculated participants relied on misinformation less when the correction came from a highly credible source.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE) is a phenomenon... The main goal of this paper is to investigate to what extent this effect can be reduced...
judge.reason: O artigo trata claramente do efeito de influência continuada, é um experimento com participantes humanos medindo crença, o método extraído corresponde ao resumo, e o achado principal é diretamente sustentado pelo trecho 'inoculated participants relied on misinformation less when the correction came from a highly credible source'.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) usando paradigma de segmentação de eventos. Relata dois experientos com manipulação neutra, sem conotação política ou de saúe. O achado extraído (nenhum efeito no Experiento 1, redução do CIE no Experiento 2) é fiel ao resumo.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies and two different CIE measures, we found that alternative provision consistently resulted in CIE reduction.
judge.evidence_topic: The term “continued influence effect” (CIE) refers to the phenomenon that discredited and obsolete information continues to affect behavior and beliefs.
judge.reason: O resumo trata explicitamente do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) em contextos de correção de desinformação, sem menção a temas políticos, eleitorais, vacinas ou COVID-19. O tipo e o método extraídos são consistentes com o resumo, e o achado principal está integralmente respaldado pelo trecho citado.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.evidence_topic: using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.reason: O artigo relata experimentos online que medem o efeito de influência continuada com materiais neutros (relatos de um evento inventado, sem conotação política ou de saúde), conforme exigido pelo pedido. items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.

items.title: Listening to misinformation while driving: Cognitive load and the effectiveness of (repeated) corrections.

judge.evidence_empirical: Trecho do resumo: "Participants listened to corrections that repeated misinformation while in a driving simulator. [...] Multiple corrections were more effective than a single correction; cognitive load reduced correction effectiveness..."

judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de influência continuada, relata um experimento com participantes humanos, e o achado principal extraí do condiz integralmente com o resumo.

items.title: Correcting the unknown: Negated corrections may increase belief in misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Trecho do resumo: "Subjets leram uma (Experimento 1) ou seis (Experimento 2) passagens apresentando um conceito-alvo (por exemplo, carro azul) ou não, seguidas de uma correção negada (por exemplo, não azul), substituição (por exemplo, vermelho) ou nenhuma correção, depois responderam a perguntas abertas que foram pontuadas por menções ao conceito-alvo." Isso descreve experimentos com coleta de dados próprios.
judge.evidence_topic: Trecho do resumo: "Negated corrections, which state a piece of information is not true, may only be effective at inhibiting information an observer has already encountered. ... These results demonstrate that negated corrections can increase belief in misinformation when observers have not been exposed to the misinformation." O artigo investiga o efeito de correções sobre a crença em desinformação, tema central do efeito de influência continuada, usando cenários neutros (ex.: carro azul) e sem conotação política ou de saúde.
judge.reason: O estudo relata um experimento empírico que investiga o efeito de correções sobre a crença em desinformação, alinhado ao pedido. O tipo de estudo e método estão corretos. O achado extraído é fielmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted. Person impressions were recorded after the presentation of each behaviour description.
judge.evidence_topic: Despite robust evidence that misinformation continues to influence event-related reasoning after a clear retraction, evidence for the continued influence of misinformation on person impressions is mixed. Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada, com materiais neutros (protagonista fictício). É estudo empírico com quatro experimentos, dados próprios. Método e tipo de estudo extraídos batem com o resumo. Achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Did he or didn’t he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

items.title: Do false allegations persist? Retracted misinformation does not continue to influence explicit person impressions.

judge.reason: O resumo afirma explicitamente que a alegação desmentida não influenciou avaliações de traços nem previsões de comportamento, e que houve apenas evidência tentativa de influência em uma medida indireta. O achado principal extraído sintetiza corretamente esses resultados.

items.title: Sensitivity to misinformation retractions in the continued influence paradigm: Evidence for stability

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants were given parallel forms of a standard CIE task 4 weeks apart, and the association between testing points was assessed with an intra-class correlation coefficient and confirmatory factor analysis.

items.title: How Stories in Memory Perpetuate the Continued Influence of False Information

judge.evidence_empirical: The current work shows that the continued influence effect depends on the stories people have in memory: corrected misinformation was found to have a stronger effect on people's beliefs than information that was topically related to the story if it helped to provide a causal explanation of a story they had read previously.
judge.evidence_topic: People often encounter information that they subsequently learn is false. Past research has shown that people sometimes continue to use this misinformation in their reasoning, even if they remember that the information is false, which researchers refer to as the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o continued influence effect, medindo crença após correção, com experimentos e materiais neutros, conforme exigido. O resumo confirma estudo empírico com dados próprios, e o achado extraído é fiel ao trecho que o sustenta.
